catalog_quote: Results indicate that stress is realized on the ultima with a raised fundamental frequency, greater intensity, and longer duration. ... 1. Is stress, which, based on the judgements of the author, impressionistically falls on the ultimate syllable of the word, regularly associated with all or any of the traditional acoustic correlates of stress (e.g., intensity, duration, fundamental frequency)? ... While there are no previous studies devoted to Besemah prosody, Helfrich, in his section on Besemah phonology, describes stress in the following way, ‘[t]he accent is, in contrast to the one in Malay, quite strong and falls on the penultimate syllable, even in derived words. . . . However, if the penultimate syllable has the atonic “@” and if it is not closed then the accent falls on the ultimate syllable’ (1904: 200). audit.reasoning: (1) Quote check: every fragment of the deciding quotation is verbatim in the held NUSA 60 PDF at the stated pages (p.1 abstract, p.4 RQ1/RQ2, p.5 Helfrich vs author's judgement, p.7 prepenultimate schwa). (2) Deciding source is a 2016 instrumental study by the language's principal describer, corroborated by his dissertation sketch (p.27: final stress, shifting onto suffixes/enclitics) and the 2018 Speech Prosody paper — all held. Glottolog's 15 descriptive refs for cent2053 are Helfrich's 1904-1933 Dutch materials and Indonesian morphology/syntax sketches of the various South Barisan lects; none is a better stress source, and web search found no JIPA Illustration or later prosodic study. (3) fetched sources now: Helfrich 1904 original (archive.org; p.200-201 confirms McDonnell's rendering of the historical penult rule, already captured in srule) and the Kaufman & Himmelmann handbook chapter draf

sources.citation: Helfrich, O. L. 1904. Bijdragen tot de kennis van het Midden Maleisch (Besemahsch en Serawajsch dialect). Verhandelingen van het Bataviaasch Genootschap van Kunsten en Wetenschappen 53. Batavia: Landsdrukkerij.
sources.quote: 'De klemtoon is in tegenstelling met die in het Maleisch vrij sterk en valt op de voorlaatste lettergreep, zelfs in afgeleide woorden, welke door een aanhechtsel langer zijn geworden dan het stamwoord. Heeft echter de voorlaatste lettergreep de doffe "e" en is die niet gesloten dan valt de klemtoon op de laatste lettergreep als: poedji; kepoedjian; besaq; benagr ...' — i.e. penultimate accent, ultimate when the penult is an open schwa syllable. This is the 1904 historical description; McDonnell's English rendering in NUSA 60 p.5 is faithful. It contradicts the synchronic ultima coding only in
sources.note: The only pre-McDonnell stress description (penult, ultima after open schwa penult); our srule quoted it second-hand via McDonnell — now verified against the original p.200-201.
